title: A patch engine
hints: Parse into a list of `PatchSpec`, validating each patch after the whole file is read. Keep `check` as the single place that decides whether applying is safe, and have `applyAll` call it first: that is what makes it all or nothing.
Once a pattern-located patch is applied, the pattern may no longer match (you changed some of its bytes). To find it again for reverting, treat the replaced positions of the pattern as wildcards.
requirements: The patch file format is parsed with clear errors for each kind of mistake.
Patches are located by offset or by a unique pattern match.
Every problem is found before anything is written; applying is all or nothing.
Reverting restores the original bytes exactly, and refuses if the code is not in the patched state.
stretch: Make the engine work on a real file: load an `.exe` you built, convert each patch's offset from an RVA with your PE inspector of milestone 1, write the patched copy beside the original, and keep a log of what was changed.
